Isa.66.3.bsb: Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who slays a man; whoever sacrifices a lamb is like one who breaks a dog’s neck; whoever presents a grain offering is like one who offers pig’s blood; whoever offers frankincense is like one who blesses an idol. Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.
Isa.66.3.kjv: He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog’s neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine’s blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol. Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations.

Isa.34.7.bsb: And the wild oxen will fall with them, the young bulls with the strong ones. Their land will be drenched with blood, and their soil will be soaked with fat.
Isa.34.7.kjv: And the unicorns shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.

Isa.58.1.bsb: “Cry aloud, do not hold back! Raise your voice like a ram’s horn. Declare to My people their transgression and to the house of Jacob their sins.
Isa.58.1.kjv: Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins.

Isa.21.8.bsb: Then the lookout shouted: “Day after day, my lord, I stand on the watchtower; night after night I stay at my post.
Isa.21.8.kjv: And he cried, A lion: My lord, I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime, and I am set in my ward whole nights:

Isa.7.2.bsb: When it was reported to the house of David that Aram was in league with Ephraim, the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaken by the wind.
Isa.7.2.kjv: And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.

Isa.14.1.bsb: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob; once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.
Isa.14.1.kjv: For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.

Isa.14.7.bsb: All the earth is at peace and at rest; they break out in song.
Isa.14.7.kjv: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.

Isa.23.12.bsb: He said, “You shall rejoice no more, O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon. Get up and cross over to Cyprus—even there you will find no rest.”
Isa.23.12.kjv: And he said, Thou shalt no more rejoice, O thou oppressed virgin, daughter of Zidon: arise, pass over to Chittim; there also shalt thou have no rest.

Isa.25.10.bsb: For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain. But Moab will be trampled in his place as straw is trodden into the dung pile.
Isa.25.10.kjv: For in this mountain shall the hand of the Lord rest, and Moab shall be trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill.

Isa.37.4.bsb: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and He will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives.”
Isa.37.4.kjv: It may be the Lord thy God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master hath sent to reproach the living God, and will reprove the words which the Lord thy God hath heard: wherefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that is left.

Isa.5.8.bsb: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.
Isa.5.8.kjv: Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!

Isa.8.8.bsb: It will pour into Judah, swirling and sweeping over it, reaching up to the neck; its spreading streams will cover your entire land, O Immanuel!
Isa.8.8.kjv: And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.

Isa.16.8.bsb: For the fields of Heshbon have withered, along with the grapevines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines, which had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Their shoots had spread out and passed over the sea.
Isa.16.8.kjv: For the fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah: the lords of the heathen have broken down the principal plants thereof, they are come even unto Jazer, they wandered through the wilderness: her branches are stretched out, they are gone over the sea.

Isa.25.12.bsb: The high-walled fortress will be brought down, cast to the ground, into the dust.
Isa.25.12.kjv: And the fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust.

Isa.26.5.bsb: For He has humbled those who dwell on high; He lays the lofty city low. He brings it down to the ground; He casts it into the dust.
Isa.26.5.kjv: For he bringeth down them that dwell on high; the lofty city, he layeth it low; he layeth it low, even to the ground; he bringeth it even to the dust.

Isa.24.19.bsb: The earth is utterly broken apart, the earth is split open, the earth is shaken violently.
Isa.24.19.kjv: The earth is utterly broken down, the earth is clean dissolved, the earth is moved exceedingly.

Isa.10.10.bsb: As my hand seized the idolatrous kingdoms whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
Isa.10.10.kjv: As my hand hath found the kingdoms of the idols, and whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem and of Samaria;

Isa.34.17.bsb: He has allotted their portion; His hand has distributed it by measure. They will possess it forever; they will dwell in it from generation to generation.
Isa.34.17.kjv: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.

Isa.41.7.bsb: The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and he who wields the hammer cheers him who strikes the anvil, saying of the welding, “It is good.” He nails it down so it will not be toppled.
Isa.41.7.kjv: So the carpenter encouraged the goldsmith, and he that smootheth with the hammer him that smote the anvil, saying, It is ready for the sodering: and he fastened it with nails, that it should not be moved.

Isa.16.7.bsb: Therefore let Moab wail; let them wail together for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, you who are utterly stricken.
Isa.16.7.kjv: Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kir–hareseth shall ye mourn; surely they are stricken.

Isa.41.16.bsb: You will winnow them, and a wind will carry them away; a gale will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
Isa.41.16.kjv: Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them: and thou shalt rejoice in the Lord, and shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel.

Isa.10.19.bsb: The remaining trees of its forests will be so few that a child could count them.
Isa.10.19.kjv: And the rest of the trees of his forest shall be few, that a child may write them.

Isa.10.34.bsb: He will clear the forest thickets with an axe, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
Isa.10.34.kjv: And he shall cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one.

Isa.29.17.bsb: In a very short time, will not Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest?
Isa.29.17.kjv: Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest?

Isa.56.9.bsb: Come, all you beasts of the field; eat greedily, all you beasts of the forest.
Isa.56.9.kjv: All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, yea, all ye beasts in the forest.

Isa.53.8.bsb: By oppression and judgment He was taken away, and who can recount His descendants? For He was cut off from the land of the living; He was stricken for the transgression of My people.
Isa.53.8.kjv: He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.

Isa.19.18.bsb: In that day five cities in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of Hosts. One of them will be called the City of the Sun.
Isa.19.18.kjv: In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.

Isa.23.8.bsb: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders are princes, whose merchants are renowned on the earth?
Isa.23.8.kjv: Who hath taken this counsel against Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth?

Isa.13.8.bsb: Terror, pain, and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another, their faces flushed with fear.
Isa.13.8.kjv: And they shall be afraid: pangs and sorrows shall take hold of them; they shall be in pain as a woman that travaileth: they shall be amazed one at another; their faces shall be as flames.

Isa.3.25.bsb: Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
Isa.3.25.kjv: Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.

Isa.21.17.bsb: The remaining archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
Isa.21.17.kjv: And the residue of the number of archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, shall be diminished: for the Lord God of Israel hath spoken it.

Isa.7.13.bsb: Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of men? Will you try the patience of my God as well?
Isa.7.13.kjv: And he said, Hear ye now, O house of David; Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also?

Isa.10.25.bsb: For in just a little while My fury against you will subside, and My anger will turn to their destruction.”
Isa.10.25.kjv: For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall cease, and mine anger in their destruction.

Isa.16.14.bsb: And now the LORD says, “In three years, as a hired worker counts the years, Moab’s splendor will become an object of contempt, with all her many people. And those who are left will be few and feeble.”
Isa.16.14.kjv: But now the Lord hath spoken, saying, Within three years, as the years of an hireling, and the glory of Moab shall be contemned, with all that great multitude; and the remnant shall be very small and feeble.

Isa.23.7.bsb: Is this your jubilant city, whose origin is from antiquity, whose feet have taken her to settle far away?
Isa.23.7.kjv: Is this your joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days? her own feet shall carry her afar off to sojourn.

Isa.13.19.bsb: And Babylon, the jewel of the kingdoms, the glory of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be overthrown by God like Sodom and Gomorrah.
Isa.13.19.kjv: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

Isa.14.16.bsb: Those who see you will stare; they will ponder your fate: “Is this the man who shook the earth and made the kingdoms tremble,
Isa.14.16.kjv: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms;

Isa.19.2.bsb: “So I will incite Egyptian against Egyptian; brother will fight against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
Isa.19.2.kjv: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.

Isa.47.5.bsb: “Sit in silence and go into darkness, O Daughter of the Chaldeans. For you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
Isa.47.5.kjv: Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called, The lady of kingdoms.

Isa.33.6.bsb: He will be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
Isa.33.6.kjv: And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.

Isa.23.4.bsb: Be ashamed, O Sidon, the stronghold of the sea, for the sea has spoken: “I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
Isa.23.4.kjv: Be thou ashamed, O Zidon: for the sea hath spoken, even the strength of the sea, saying, I travail not, nor bring forth children, neither do I nourish up young men, nor bring up virgins.

Isa.23.5.bsb: When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe in agony over the news of Tyre.
Isa.23.5.kjv: As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre.

Isa.45.10.bsb: Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What have you begotten?’ or to his mother, ‘What have you brought forth?’”
Isa.45.10.kjv: Woe unto him that saith unto his father, What begettest thou? or to the woman, What hast thou brought forth?

Isa.43.19.bsb: Behold, I am about to do something new; even now it is coming. Do you not see it? Indeed, I will make a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
Isa.43.19.kjv: Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

Isa.13.11.bsb: I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. I will end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless.
Isa.13.11.kjv: And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.

Isa.14.17.bsb: who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who refused to let the captives return to their homes?”
Isa.14.17.kjv: That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof; that opened not the house of his prisoners?

Isa.24.4.bsb: The earth mourns and withers; the world languishes and fades; the exalted of the earth waste away.
Isa.24.4.kjv: The earth mourneth and fadeth away, the world languisheth and fadeth away, the haughty people of the earth do languish.

Isa.27.6.bsb: In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
Isa.27.6.kjv: He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit.

Isa.34.1.bsb: Come near, O nations, to listen; pay attention, O peoples. Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and all that springs from it.
Isa.34.1.kjv: Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye people: let the earth hear, and all that is therein; the world, and all things that come forth of it.

Isa.22.16.bsb: What are you doing here, and who authorized you to carve out a tomb for yourself here—to chisel your tomb in the height and cut your resting place in the rock?
Isa.22.16.kjv: What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, as he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high, and that graveth an habitation for himself in a rock?

Isa.14.14.bsb: I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.”
Isa.14.14.kjv: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.

Isa.36.7.bsb: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before this altar’?
Isa.36.7.kjv: But if thou say to me, We trust in the Lord our God: is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?

Isa.10.22.bsb: Though your people, O Israel, be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
Isa.10.22.kjv: For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.

Isa.49.2.bsb: He made My mouth like a sharp sword; He hid Me in the shadow of His hand. He made Me like a polished arrow; He hid Me in His quiver.
Isa.49.2.kjv: And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me;

Isa.36.6.bsb: Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
Isa.36.6.kjv: Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him.

Isa.14.13.bsb: You said in your heart: “I will ascend to the heavens; I will raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.
Isa.14.13.kjv: For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:

Isa.16.5.bsb: in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David. A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on it in faithfulness.
Isa.16.5.kjv: And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness.

Isa.47.1.bsb: “Go down and sit in the dust, O Virgin Daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground without a throne, O Daughter of the Chaldeans! For you will no longer be called tender or delicate.
Isa.47.1.kjv: Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.

Isa.39.3.bsb: Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and asked, “Where did those men come from, and what did they say to you?” “They came to me from a distant land,” Hezekiah replied, “from Babylon.”
Isa.39.3.kjv: Then came Isaiah the prophet unto king Hezekiah, and said unto him, What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee? And Hezekiah said, They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon.

Isa.49.1.bsb: Listen to Me, O islands; pay attention, O distant peoples: The LORD called Me from the womb; from the body of My mother He named Me.
Isa.49.1.kjv: Listen, O isles, unto me; and hearken, ye people, from far; The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name.

Isa.38.8.bsb: I will make the sun’s shadow that falls on the stairway of Ahaz go back ten steps.’” So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended.
Isa.38.8.kjv: Behold, I will bring again the shadow of the degrees, which is gone down in the sun dial of Ahaz, ten degrees backward. So the sun returned ten degrees, by which degrees it was gone down.

Isa.14.10.bsb: They will all respond to you, saying, “You too have become weak, as we are; you have become like us!”
Isa.14.10.kjv: All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?

Isa.41.25.bsb: I have raised up one from the north, and he has come—one from the east who calls on My name. He will march over rulers as if they were mortar, like a potter who treads the clay.
Isa.41.25.kjv: I have raised up one from the north, and he shall come: from the rising of the sun shall he call upon my name: and he shall come upon princes as upon morter, and as the potter treadeth clay.

Isa.7.9.bsb: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.’”
Isa.7.9.kjv: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

Isa.10.15.bsb: Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it? Does a saw boast over him who saws with it? It would be like a rod waving the one who lifts it, or a staff lifting him who is not wood!
Isa.10.15.kjv: Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith? or shall the saw magnify itself against him that shaketh it? as if the rod should shake itself against them that lift it up, or as if the staff should lift up itself, as if it were no wood.

Isa.42.21.bsb: The LORD was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify His law and make it glorious.
Isa.42.21.kjv: The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.

Isa.27.10.bsb: For the fortified city lies deserted—a homestead abandoned, a wilderness forsaken. There the calves graze, and there they lie down; they strip its branches bare.
Isa.27.10.kjv: Yet the defenced city shall be desolate, and the habitation forsaken, and left like a wilderness: there shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof.

Isa.34.13.bsb: Her towers will be overgrown with thorns, her fortresses with thistles and briers. She will become a haunt for jackals, an abode for ostriches.
Isa.34.13.kjv: And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons, and a court for owls.

Isa.33.4.bsb: Your spoil, O nations, is gathered as by locusts; like a swarm of locusts men sweep over it.
Isa.33.4.kjv: And your spoil shall be gathered like the gathering of the caterpiller: as the running to and fro of locusts shall he run upon them.

Isa.48.4.bsb: For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze.
Isa.48.4.kjv: Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass;

Isa.11.14.bsb: They will swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west; together they will plunder the sons of the east. They will lay their hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will be subject to them.
Isa.11.14.kjv: But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west; they shall spoil them of the east together: they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

Isa.36.10.bsb: So now, was it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’”
Isa.36.10.kjv: And am I now come up without the Lord against this land to destroy it? the Lord said unto me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

Isa.40.1.bsb: “Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.
Isa.40.1.kjv: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.

Isa.13.7.bsb: Therefore all hands will fall limp, and every man’s heart will melt.
Isa.13.7.kjv: Therefore shall all hands be faint, and every man’s heart shall melt:

Isa.21.10.bsb: O my people, crushed on the threshing floor, I tell you what I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel.
Isa.21.10.kjv: O my threshing, and the corn of my floor: that which I have heard of the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, have I declared unto you.

Isa.15.3.bsb: In its streets they wear sackcloth; on the rooftops and in the public squares they all wail, falling down weeping.
Isa.15.3.kjv: In their streets they shall gird themselves with sackcloth: on the tops of their houses, and in their streets, every one shall howl, weeping abundantly.

Isa.58.5.bsb: Is this the fast I have chosen: a day for a man to deny himself, to bow his head like a reed, and to spread out sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast and a day acceptable to the LORD?
Isa.58.5.kjv: Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the Lord?

Isa.21.4.bsb: My heart falters; fear makes me tremble. The twilight I desired has turned to horror.
Isa.21.4.kjv: My heart panted, fearfulness affrighted me: the night of my pleasure hath he turned into fear unto me.

Isa.20.5.bsb: Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed.
Isa.20.5.kjv: And they shall be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.

Isa.30.31.bsb: For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD; He will strike them with His scepter.
Isa.30.31.kjv: For through the voice of the Lord shall the Assyrian be beaten down, which smote with a rod.

Isa.48.10.bsb: See, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
Isa.48.10.kjv: Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.

Isa.24.22.bsb: They will be gathered together like prisoners in a pit. They will be confined to a dungeon and punished after many days.
Isa.24.22.kjv: And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited.

Isa.47.9.bsb: These two things will overtake you in a moment, in a single day: loss of children, and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the potency of your spells.
Isa.47.9.kjv: But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.

Isa.7.11.bsb: “Ask for a sign from the LORD your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven.”
Isa.7.11.kjv: Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.

Isa.63.15.bsb: Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation. Where are Your zeal and might? Your yearning and compassion for me are restrained.
Isa.63.15.kjv: Look down from heaven, and behold from the habitation of thy holiness and of thy glory: where is thy zeal and thy strength, the sounding of thy bowels and of thy mercies toward me? are they restrained?

Isa.22.17.bsb: Look, O mighty man! The LORD is about to shake you violently. He will take hold of you,
Isa.22.17.kjv: Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee.

Isa.10.3.bsb: What will you do on the day of reckoning when devastation comes from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
Isa.10.3.kjv: And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory?

Isa.15.7.bsb: So they carry their wealth and belongings over the Brook of the Willows.
Isa.15.7.kjv: Therefore the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have laid up, shall they carry away to the brook of the willows.

Isa.15.5.bsb: My heart cries out over Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. With weeping they ascend the slope of Luhith; they lament their destruction on the road to Horonaim.
Isa.15.5.kjv: My heart shall cry out for Moab; his fugitives shall flee unto Zoar, an heifer of three years old: for by the mounting up of Luhith with weeping shall they go it up; for in the way of Horonaim they shall raise up a cry of destruction.

Isa.13.20.bsb: She will never be inhabited or settled from generation to generation; no nomad will pitch his tent there, no shepherd will rest his flock there.
Isa.13.20.kjv: It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their fold there.

Isa.13.21.bsb: But desert creatures will lie down there, and howling creatures will fill her houses. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about.
Isa.13.21.kjv: But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there.

Isa.34.11.bsb: The desert owl and screech owl will possess it, and the great owl and raven will dwell in it. The LORD will stretch out over Edom a measuring line of chaos and a plumb line of destruction.
Isa.34.11.kjv: But the cormorant and the bittern shall possess it; the owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the stones of emptiness.

Isa.22.19.bsb: I will remove you from office, and you will be ousted from your position.
Isa.22.19.kjv: And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.

Isa.21.3.bsb: Therefore my body is filled with anguish. Pain grips me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am bewildered to hear, I am dismayed to see.
Isa.21.3.kjv: Therefore are my loins filled with pain: pangs have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman that travaileth: I was bowed down at the hearing of it; I was dismayed at the seeing of it.

Isa.36.9.bsb: For how can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants when you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
Isa.36.9.kjv: How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

Isa.39.2.bsb: And Hezekiah welcomed the envoys gladly and showed them what was in his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, as well as his entire armory—all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.
Isa.39.2.kjv: And Hezekiah was glad of them, and shewed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and all the house of his armour, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah shewed them not.

Isa.39.4.bsb: “What have they seen in your palace?” Isaiah asked. “They have seen everything in my palace,” answered Hezekiah. “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”
Isa.39.4.kjv: Then said he, What have they seen in thine house? And Hezekiah answered, All that is in mine house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shewed them.

Isa.22.18.bsb: roll you into a ball, and sling you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your glorious chariots will remain—a disgrace to the house of your master.
Isa.22.18.kjv: He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord’s house.

Isa.19.8.bsb: Then the fishermen will mourn, all who cast a hook into the Nile will lament, and those who spread nets on the waters will pine away.
Isa.19.8.kjv: The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the brooks shall lament, and they that spread nets upon the waters shall languish.

Isa.25.11.bsb: He will spread out his hands within it, as a swimmer spreads his arms to swim. His pride will be brought low, despite the skill of his hands.
Isa.25.11.kjv: And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim: and he shall bring down their pride together with the spoils of their hands.

Isa.13.2.bsb: Raise a banner on a barren hilltop; call aloud to them. Wave your hand, that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
Isa.13.2.kjv: Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

Isa.14.2.bsb: The nations will escort Israel and bring it to its homeland. Then the house of Israel will possess the nations as menservants and maidservants in the LORD’s land. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
Isa.14.2.kjv: And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

Isa.19.6.bsb: The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will trickle and dry up; the reeds and rushes will wither.
Isa.19.6.kjv: And they shall turn the rivers far away; and the brooks of defence shall be emptied and dried up: the reeds and flags shall wither.

Isa.10.13.bsb: For he says: ‘By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am clever. I have removed the boundaries of nations and plundered their treasures; like a mighty one I subdued their rulers.
Isa.10.13.kjv: For he saith, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the inhabitants like a valiant man:

Isa.13.12.bsb: I will make man scarcer than pure gold, and mankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
Isa.13.12.kjv: I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.

Isa.36.5.bsb: You claim to have a strategy and strength for war, but these are empty words. In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?
Isa.36.5.kjv: I say, sayest thou, (but they are but vain words) I have counsel and strength for war: now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?

Isa.34.10.bsb: It will not be quenched—day or night. Its smoke will ascend forever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; no one will ever again pass through it.
Isa.34.10.kjv: It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.

Isa.14.5.bsb: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers.
Isa.14.5.kjv: The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.

Isa.16.1.bsb: Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela in the desert to the mount of Daughter Zion.
Isa.16.1.kjv: Send ye the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.

Isa.20.6.bsb: And on that day the dwellers of this coastland will say, ‘See what has happened to our source of hope, those to whom we fled for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?’”
Isa.20.6.kjv: And the inhabitant of this isle shall say in that day, Behold, such is our expectation, whither we flee for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria: and how shall we escape?

Isa.36.11.bsb: Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”
Isa.36.11.kjv: Then said Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews’ language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall.

Isa.25.5.bsb: like heat in a dry land. You subdue the uproar of foreigners. As the shade of a cloud cools the heat, so the song of the ruthless is silenced.
Isa.25.5.kjv: Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers, as the heat in a dry place; even the heat with the shadow of a cloud: the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low.

Isa.17.12.bsb: Alas, the tumult of many peoples; they rage like the roaring seas and clamoring nations; they rumble like the crashing of mighty waters.
Isa.17.12.kjv: Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!

Isa.10.4.bsb: Nothing will remain but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
Isa.10.4.kjv: Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

Isa.14.6.bsb: It struck the peoples in anger with unceasing blows; it subdued the nations in rage with relentless persecution.
Isa.14.6.kjv: He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger, is persecuted, and none hindereth.

Isa.23.9.bsb: The LORD of Hosts planned it, to defile all its glorious beauty, to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
Isa.23.9.kjv: The Lord of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.

Isa.24.20.bsb: The earth staggers like a drunkard and sways like a shack. Earth’s rebellion weighs it down, and it falls, never to rise again.
Isa.24.20.kjv: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, and shall be removed like a cottage; and the transgression thereof shall be heavy upon it; and it shall fall, and not rise again.

Isa.25.3.bsb: Therefore, a strong people will honor You. The cities of ruthless nations will revere You.
Isa.25.3.kjv: Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee.

Isa.47.6.bsb: I was angry with My people; I profaned My heritage, and I placed them under your control. You showed them no mercy; even on the elderly you laid a most heavy yoke.
Isa.47.6.kjv: I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.

Isa.14.31.bsb: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke comes from the north, and there are no stragglers in its ranks.
Isa.14.31.kjv: Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou, whole Palestina, art dissolved: for there shall come from the north a smoke, and none shall be alone in his appointed times.

Isa.15.4.bsb: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the soldiers of Moab cry out; their souls tremble within.
Isa.15.4.kjv: And Heshbon shall cry, and Elealeh: their voice shall be heard even unto Jahaz: therefore the armed soldiers of Moab shall cry out; his life shall be grievous unto him.

Isa.19.22.bsb: And the LORD will strike Egypt with a plague; He will strike them but heal them. They will turn to the LORD, and He will hear their prayers and heal them.
Isa.19.22.kjv: And the Lord shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal it: and they shall return even to the Lord, and he shall be intreated of them, and shall heal them.

Isa.36.4.bsb: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah that this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?
Isa.36.4.kjv: And Rabshakeh said unto them, Say ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?

Isa.47.10.bsb: You were secure in your wickedness; you said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray; you told yourself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me.’
Isa.47.10.kjv: For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.

Isa.10.26.bsb: And the LORD of Hosts will brandish a whip against them, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise His staff over the sea, as He did in Egypt.
Isa.10.26.kjv: And the Lord of hosts shall stir up a scourge for him according to the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb: and as his rod was upon the sea, so shall he lift it up after the manner of Egypt.

Isa.13.17.bsb: Behold, I will stir up against them the Medes, who have no regard for silver and no desire for gold.
Isa.13.17.kjv: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.

Isa.50.4.bsb: The Lord GOD has given Me the tongue of discipleship, to sustain the weary with a word. He awakens Me morning by morning; He awakens My ear to listen as a disciple.
Isa.50.4.kjv: The Lord God hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned.

Isa.11.15.bsb: The LORD will devote to destruction the gulf of the Sea of Egypt; with a scorching wind He will sweep His hand over the Euphrates. He will split it into seven streams for men to cross with dry sandals.
Isa.11.15.kjv: And the Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his mighty wind shall he shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in the seven streams, and make men go over dryshod.

Isa.18.1.bsb: Woe to the land of whirring wings, along the rivers of Cush,
Isa.18.1.kjv: Woe to the land shadowing with wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia:

Isa.18.2.bsb: which sends couriers by sea, in papyrus vessels on the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a people tall and smooth-skinned, to a people widely feared, to a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers.
Isa.18.2.kjv: That sendeth ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of bulrushes upon the waters, saying, Go, ye swift messengers, to a nation scattered and peeled, to a people terrible from their beginning hitherto; a nation meted out and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled!

Isa.19.5.bsb: The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.
Isa.19.5.kjv: And the waters shall fail from the sea, and the river shall be wasted and dried up.

Isa.27.12.bsb: In that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.
Isa.27.12.kjv: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.

Isa.42.15.bsb: I will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation. I will turn the rivers into dry land and drain the marshes.
Isa.42.15.kjv: I will make waste mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs; and I will make the rivers islands, and I will dry up the pools.

Isa.47.2.bsb: Take millstones and grind flour; remove your veil; strip off your skirt, bare your thigh, and wade through the streams.
Isa.47.2.kjv: Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers.

Isa.48.18.bsb: If only you had paid attention to My commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like waves of the sea.
Isa.48.18.kjv: O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea:

Isa.34.14.bsb: The desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and one wild goat will call to another. There the night creature will settle and find her place of repose.
Isa.34.14.kjv: The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the wild beasts of the island, and the satyr shall cry to his fellow; the screech owl also shall rest there, and find for herself a place of rest.

Isa.37.8.bsb: When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.
Isa.37.8.kjv: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah: for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish.

Isa.10.29.bsb: They have crossed at the ford: “We will spend the night at Geba.” Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul flees.
Isa.10.29.kjv: They are gone over the passage: they have taken up their lodging at Geba; Ramah is afraid; Gibeah of Saul is fled.

Isa.10.30.bsb: Cry aloud, O Daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! O wretched Anathoth!
Isa.10.30.kjv: Lift up thy voice, O daughter of Gallim: cause it to be heard unto Laish, O poor Anathoth.

Isa.39.6.bsb: The time will surely come when everything in your palace and all that your fathers have stored up until this day will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
Isa.39.6.kjv: Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord.

Isa.33.9.bsb: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and decayed. Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
Isa.33.9.kjv: The earth mourneth and languisheth: Lebanon is ashamed and hewn down: Sharon is like a wilderness; and Bashan and Carmel shake off their fruits.

Isa.22.20.bsb: On that day I will summon My servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
Isa.22.20.kjv: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:

Isa.23.13.bsb: Look at the land of the Chaldeans—a people now of no account. The Assyrians destined it for the desert creatures; they set up their siege towers and stripped its palaces. They brought it to ruin.
Isa.23.13.kjv: Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not, till the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness: they set up the towers thereof, they raised up the palaces thereof; and he brought it to ruin.

Isa.22.22.bsb: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.
Isa.22.22.kjv: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.

Isa.5.11.bsb: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.
Isa.5.11.kjv: Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them!

Isa.51.21.bsb: Therefore now hear this, you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine.
Isa.51.21.kjv: Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine:

Isa.56.12.bsb: “Come, let me get the wine, let us imbibe the strong drink, and tomorrow will be like today, only far better!”
Isa.56.12.kjv: Come ye, say they, I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and to morrow shall be as this day, and much more abundant.

Isa.24.7.bsb: The new wine dries up, the vine withers. All the merrymakers now groan.
Isa.24.7.kjv: The new wine mourneth, the vine languisheth, all the merryhearted do sigh.

Isa.7.6.bsb: ‘Let us invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among ourselves. Then we can install the son of Tabeal over it as king.’
Isa.7.6.kjv: Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the midst of it, even the son of Tabeal:

Isa.21.7.bsb: When he sees chariots with teams of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, he must be alert, fully alert.”
Isa.21.7.kjv: And he saw a chariot with a couple of horsemen, a chariot of asses, and a chariot of camels; and he hearkened diligently with much heed:

Isa.19.19.bsb: In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the center of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD near her border.
Isa.19.19.kjv: In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.

Isa.7.12.bsb: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask; I will not test the LORD.”
Isa.7.12.kjv: But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord.

Isa.36.2.bsb: And the king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh, with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. And he stopped by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
Isa.36.2.kjv: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field.

Isa.39.8.bsb: But Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “At least there will be peace and security in my lifetime.”
Isa.39.8.kjv: Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days.

Isa.37.7.bsb: Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword.’”
Isa.37.7.kjv: Behold, I will send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a rumour, and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.

Isa.58.2.bsb: For day after day they seek Me and delight to know My ways, like a nation that does what is right and does not forsake the justice of their God. They ask Me for righteous judgments; they delight in the nearness of God.”
Isa.58.2.kjv: Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and forsook not the ordinance of their God: they ask of me the ordinances of justice; they take delight in approaching to God.

Isa.58.3.bsb: “Why have we fasted, and You have not seen? Why have we humbled ourselves, and You have not noticed?” “Behold, on the day of your fast, you do as you please, and you oppress all your workers.
Isa.58.3.kjv: Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge? Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours.

Isa.56.11.bsb: Like ravenous dogs, they are never satisfied. They are shepherds with no discernment; they all turn to their own way, each one seeking his own gain:
Isa.56.11.kjv: Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter.

Isa.26.6.bsb: Feet trample it down—the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.
Isa.26.6.kjv: The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy.

Isa.7.5.bsb: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted your ruin, saying:
Isa.7.5.kjv: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against thee, saying,

Isa.34.5.bsb: When My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens, then it will come down upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to destruction.
Isa.34.5.kjv: For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.

Isa.34.6.bsb: The sword of the LORD is bathed in blood. It drips with fat—with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
Isa.34.6.kjv: The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea.

Isa.34.3.bsb: Their slain will be left unburied, and the stench of their corpses will rise; the mountains will flow with their blood.
Isa.34.3.kjv: Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stink shall come up out of their carcases, and the mountains shall be melted with their blood.

Isa.18.5.bsb: For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with a pruning knife and remove and discard the branches.
Isa.18.5.kjv: For afore the harvest, when the bud is perfect, and the sour grape is ripening in the flower, he shall both cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and take away and cut down the branches.

Isa.10.9.bsb: “Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
Isa.10.9.kjv: Is not Calno as Carchemish? is not Hamath as Arpad? is not Samaria as Damascus?

Isa.7.16.bsb: For before the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.
Isa.7.16.kjv: For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings.

Isa.7.1.bsb: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.
Isa.7.1.kjv: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

Isa.13.22.bsb: Hyenas will howl in her fortresses and jackals in her luxurious palaces. Babylon’s time is at hand, and her days will not be prolonged.
Isa.13.22.kjv: And the wild beasts of the islands shall cry in their desolate houses, and dragons in their pleasant palaces: and her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.

Isa.47.8.bsb: So now hear this, O lover of luxury who sits securely, who says to herself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me. I will never be a widow or know the loss of children.’
Isa.47.8.kjv: Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:

Isa.24.10.bsb: The city of chaos is shattered; every house is closed to entry.
Isa.24.10.kjv: The city of confusion is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in.

Isa.41.15.bsb: Behold, I will make you into a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and reduce the hills to chaff.
Isa.41.15.kjv: Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff.

Isa.3.6.bsb: A man will seize his brother within his father’s house: “You have a cloak—you be our leader! Take charge of this heap of rubble.”
Isa.3.6.kjv: When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand:

Isa.36.1.bsb: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
Isa.36.1.kjv: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them.

Isa.15.9.bsb: The waters of Dimon are full of blood, but I will bring more upon Dimon—a lion upon the fugitives of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
Isa.15.9.kjv: For the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood: for I will bring more upon Dimon, lions upon him that escapeth of Moab, and upon the remnant of the land.

Isa.14.25.bsb: I will break Assyria in My land; I will trample him on My mountain. His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders.”
Isa.14.25.kjv: That I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders.

Isa.21.2.bsb: A dire vision is declared to me: “The traitor still betrays, and the destroyer still destroys. Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media! I will put an end to all her groaning.”
Isa.21.2.kjv: A grievous vision is declared unto me; the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth. Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media; all the sighing thereof have I made to cease.

Isa.27.1.bsb: In that day the LORD will take His sharp, great, and mighty sword, and bring judgment on Leviathan the fleeing serpent—Leviathan the coiling serpent—and He will slay the dragon of the sea.
Isa.27.1.kjv: In that day the Lord with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.

Isa.27.8.bsb: By warfare and exile You contended with her and removed her with a fierce wind, as on the day the east wind blows.
Isa.27.8.kjv: In measure, when it shooteth forth, thou wilt debate with it: he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind.

Isa.3.3.bsb: the commander of fifty and the dignitary, the counselor, the cunning magician, and the clever enchanter.
Isa.3.3.kjv: The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator.

Isa.14.26.bsb: This is the plan devised for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
Isa.14.26.kjv: This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth: and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations.

Isa.19.12.bsb: Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and reveal what the LORD of Hosts has planned against Egypt.
Isa.19.12.kjv: Where are they? where are thy wise men? and let them tell thee now, and let them know what the Lord of hosts hath purposed upon Egypt.

Isa.19.17.bsb: The land of Judah will bring terror to Egypt; whenever Judah is mentioned, Egypt will tremble over what the LORD of Hosts has planned against it.
Isa.19.17.kjv: And the land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt, every one that maketh mention thereof shall be afraid in himself, because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which he hath determined against it.

Isa.14.4.bsb: you will sing this song of contempt against the king of Babylon: How the oppressor has ceased, and how his fury has ended!
Isa.14.4.kjv: That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!

Isa.14.12.bsb: How you have fallen from heaven, O day star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, O destroyer of nations.
Isa.14.12.kjv: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!

Isa.19.11.bsb: The princes of Zoan are mere fools; Pharaoh’s wise counselors give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, “I am one of the wise, a son of eastern kings”?
Isa.19.11.kjv: Surely the princes of Zoan are fools, the counsel of the wise counsellors of Pharaoh is become brutish: how say ye unto Pharaoh, I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?

Isa.31.8.bsb: “Then Assyria will fall, but not by the sword of man; a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals. They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor.
Isa.31.8.kjv: Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him: but he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall be discomfited.

Isa.1.28.bsb: But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
Isa.1.28.kjv: And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.

Isa.66.24.bsb: “As they go forth, they will see the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm will never die, their fire will never be quenched, and they will be a horror to all mankind.”
Isa.66.24.kjv: And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.

Isa.41.5.bsb: The islands see and fear; the ends of the earth tremble. They approach and come forward.
Isa.41.5.kjv: The isles saw it, and feared; the ends of the earth were afraid, drew near, and came.

Isa.15.6.bsb: The waters of Nimrim are dried up, and the grass is withered; the vegetation is gone, and the greenery is no more.
Isa.15.6.kjv: For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate: for the hay is withered away, the grass faileth, there is no green thing.

Isa.19.7.bsb: The bulrushes by the Nile, by the mouth of the river, and all the fields sown along the Nile, will wither, blow away, and be no more.
Isa.19.7.kjv: The paper reeds by the brooks, by the mouth of the brooks, and every thing sown by the brooks, shall wither, be driven away, and be no more.

Isa.39.1.bsb: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard about Hezekiah’s illness and recovery.
Isa.39.1.kjv: At that time Merodach–baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah: for he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.

Isa.3.7.bsb: On that day he will cry aloud: “I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people!”
Isa.3.7.kjv: In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people.

Isa.36.8.bsb: Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!
Isa.36.8.kjv: Now therefore give pledges, I pray thee, to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.

Isa.50.5.bsb: The Lord GOD has opened My ears, and I have not been rebellious, nor have I turned back.
Isa.50.5.kjv: The Lord God hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back.

Isa.14.19.bsb: But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered by those slain with the sword, and dumped into a rocky pit like a carcass trampled underfoot.
Isa.14.19.kjv: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch, and as the raiment of those that are slain, thrust through with a sword, that go down to the stones of the pit; as a carcase trodden under feet.

Isa.14.29.bsb: Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken. For a viper will spring from the root of the snake, and a flying serpent from its egg.
Isa.14.29.kjv: Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent’s root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent.

Isa.33.1.bsb: Woe to you, O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed. When you have finished betraying, you will be betrayed.
Isa.33.1.kjv: Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.

Isa.14.23.bsb: “I will make her a place for owls and for swamplands; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
Isa.14.23.kjv: I will also make it a possession for the bittern, and pools of water: and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, saith the Lord of hosts.

Isa.48.19.bsb: Your descendants would have been as countless as the sand, and your offspring as numerous as its grains; their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence.”
Isa.48.19.kjv: Thy seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of thy bowels like the gravel thereof; his name should not have been cut off nor destroyed from before me.

Isa.7.15.bsb: By the time He knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey.
Isa.7.15.kjv: Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good.

Isa.10.32.bsb: Yet today they will halt at Nob, shaking a fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
Isa.10.32.kjv: As yet shall he remain at Nob that day: he shall shake his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

Isa.10.33.bsb: Behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled.
Isa.10.33.kjv: Behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, shall lop the bough with terror: and the high ones of stature shall be hewn down, and the haughty shall be humbled.

Isa.30.33.bsb: For Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.
Isa.30.33.kjv: For Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the Lord, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.

Isa.34.9.bsb: Edom’s streams will be turned to tar, and her soil to sulfur; her land will become a blazing pitch.
Isa.34.9.kjv: And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch.

Isa.16.2.bsb: Like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon:
Isa.16.2.kjv: For it shall be, that, as a wandering bird cast out of the nest, so the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon.

Isa.33.8.bsb: The highways are deserted; travel has ceased. The treaty has been broken, the witnesses are despised, and human life is disregarded.
Isa.33.8.kjv: The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: he hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth no man.

Isa.44.25.bsb: who foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense,
Isa.44.25.kjv: That frustrateth the tokens of the liars, and maketh diviners mad; that turneth wise men backward, and maketh their knowledge foolish;

Isa.30.28.bsb: His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He comes to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction; He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray.
Isa.30.28.kjv: And his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity: and there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err.

Isa.20.1.bsb: Before the year that the chief commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and attacked and captured it,
Isa.20.1.kjv: In the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,) and fought against Ashdod, and took it;

Isa.24.18.bsb: Whoever flees the sound of panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare. For the windows of heaven are open, and the foundations of the earth are shaken.
Isa.24.18.kjv: And it shall come to pass, that he who fleeth from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that cometh up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for the windows from on high are open, and the foundations of the earth do shake.

Isa.25.2.bsb: Indeed, You have made the city a heap of rubble, the fortified town a ruin. The fortress of strangers is a city no more; it will never be rebuilt.
Isa.25.2.kjv: For thou hast made of a city an heap; of a defenced city a ruin: a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built.

Isa.19.14.bsb: The LORD has poured into her a spirit of confusion. Egypt has been led astray in all she does, as a drunkard staggers through his own vomit.
Isa.19.14.kjv: The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof, as a drunken man staggereth in his vomit.

Isa.14.30.bsb: Then the firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety, but I will kill your root by famine, and your remnant will be slain.
Isa.14.30.kjv: And the firstborn of the poor shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety: and I will kill thy root with famine, and he shall slay thy remnant.

Isa.18.4.bsb: For this is what the LORD has told me: “I will quietly look on from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
Isa.18.4.kjv: For so the Lord said unto me, I will take my rest, and I will consider in my dwelling place like a clear heat upon herbs, and like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.

Isa.23.2.bsb: Be silent, O dwellers of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon, whose traders have crossed the sea.
Isa.23.2.kjv: Be still, ye inhabitants of the isle; thou whom the merchants of Zidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.

Isa.42.22.bsb: But this is a people plundered and looted, all trapped in caves or imprisoned in dungeons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say, “Send them back!”
Isa.42.22.kjv: But this is a people robbed and spoiled; they are all of them snared in holes, and they are hid in prison houses: they are for a prey, and none delivereth; for a spoil, and none saith, Restore.

Isa.41.21.bsb: “Present your case,” says the LORD. “Submit your arguments,” says the King of Jacob.
Isa.41.21.kjv: Produce your cause, saith the Lord; bring forth your strong reasons, saith the King of Jacob.

Isa.41.22.bsb: “Let them come and tell us what will happen. Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome. Or announce to us what is coming.
Isa.41.22.kjv: Let them bring them forth, and shew us what shall happen: let them shew the former things, what they be, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or declare us things for to come.

Isa.7.3.bsb: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,
Isa.7.3.kjv: Then said the Lord unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear–jashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field;

Isa.37.38.bsb: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.
Isa.37.38.kjv: And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Armenia: and Esar–haddon his son reigned in his stead.

Isa.49.24.bsb: Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered?
Isa.49.24.kjv: Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered?

Isa.5.10.bsb: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain.”
Isa.5.10.kjv: Yea, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and the seed of an homer shall yield an ephah.

Isa.47.3.bsb: Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed. I will take vengeance; I will spare no one.”
Isa.47.3.kjv: Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.

Isa.41.3.bsb: He pursues them, going on safely, hardly touching the path with his feet.
Isa.41.3.kjv: He pursued them, and passed safely; even by the way that he had not gone with his feet.

Isa.63.13.bsb: who led them through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, so that they did not stumble?
Isa.63.13.kjv: That led them through the deep, as an horse in the wilderness, that they should not stumble?

Isa.27.7.bsb: Has the LORD struck Israel as He struck her oppressors? Was she killed like those who slayed her?
Isa.27.7.kjv: Hath he smitten him, as he smote those that smote him? or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that are slain by him?

Isa.36.12.bsb: But the Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
Isa.36.12.kjv: But Rabshakeh said, Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?

Isa.42.24.bsb: Who gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They were unwilling to walk in His ways, and they would not obey His law.
Isa.42.24.kjv: Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers? did not the Lord, he against whom we have sinned? for they would not walk in his ways, neither were they obedient unto his law.

Isa.39.7.bsb: And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
Isa.39.7.kjv: And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

Isa.13.6.bsb: Wail, for the Day of the LORD is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
Isa.13.6.kjv: Howl ye; for the day of the Lord is at hand; it shall come as a destruction from the Almighty.

Isa.13.18.bsb: Their bows will dash young men to pieces; they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb; they will not look with pity on the children.
Isa.13.18.kjv: Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.

Isa.21.15.bsb: For they flee from the sword—the sword that is drawn—from the bow that is bent, and from the stress of battle.
Isa.21.15.kjv: For they fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, and from the bent bow, and from the grievousness of war.

Isa.13.10.bsb: For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light. The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
Isa.13.10.kjv: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine.

Isa.37.37.bsb: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
Isa.37.37.kjv: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.

Isa.10.14.bsb: My hand reached as into a nest to seize the wealth of the nations. Like one gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth. No wing fluttered, no beak opened or chirped.’”
Isa.10.14.kjv: And my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people: and as one gathereth eggs that are left, have I gathered all the earth; and there was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or peeped.

Isa.15.8.bsb: For their outcry echoes to the border of Moab. Their wailing reaches Eglaim; it is heard in Beer-elim.
Isa.15.8.kjv: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; the howling thereof unto Eglaim, and the howling thereof unto Beer–elim.

Isa.42.23.bsb: Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and obey hereafter?
Isa.42.23.kjv: Who among you will give ear to this? who will hearken and hear for the time to come?
